tasks.title: Closing-review round 2: bounce routing, composed preflight line, one return per task
tasks.summary: Factory-level. A `grader-invalid` goes to the grader's turn, never `gate run`, and a blocked gate bounces to the builder whose output its reason names (the tester for screenshots); `bs brief compose` writes each worker's filled, shell-quoted preflight line (the tester's own result file) and the gate's check commands, heavy ones marked for the heavy-run section, refusing a brief without them, and `bs dispatch lint` fails a coder, tester or grader brief without them; wave.md and queue-and-gate.md bound branch 4 at one return per task in one shared sentence.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix for the three findings of the closing spec review, round 2, on plan v5 (bs-gate-bounce-run-2026-10-29#189, judge report #190, integration head c917a05b): f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-fdeb317e (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2afed53d (S4). Line numbers are at that head; the symbol named beside each is the reference if a line has moved. Task-7's design stays: the five branches of wave.md step 7, the `input` labels, the precedence and the tie-break; this task changes only what is named here. (a) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b. wave.md step 7 branch 3 (wave.md:311-317) sends `grader-invalid`, `screenshots-missing` and `screenshots-stale` to `gate run` beside the coder's reasons; step 9 (wave.md:470) and the wave rule 'A blocked task blocks itself' (wave.md:128) bounce every blocked outcome to the coder; queue-and-gate.md's outcome table (queue-and-gate.md:461-470) says a `grader-invalid` block is answered by re-running the grading pass and has no row for the screenshots reasons. What the code does at c917a05b: `readFailedRounds` (escalation.ts:169) counts every blocked `gate-outcome` whatever its reason; `checkModelTierRung` (escalation.ts:266) compares the last builder dispatch before the failed round with the first one after it, of any role in `BUILDER_ROLES` (coder, tester, uiux; escalation.ts:47), and a grader dispatch is a judge turn, never one of them. So a screenshots block bounced to the tester is a counted round whose tier rung a tester dispatch on a higher tier answers, with no code change; but a `grader-invalid` sent to `gate run` is a counted round that only a grader turn can answer, and from the second such round the ladder demands a higher-tier builder dispatch for a fault no builder made. `gate run --grader` also closes the grader's judge turn before the gate blocks (judges.ts `graderFindingCount` accepts any document whose `structured_output.criteria` is an array), so afterwards the grader can only be re-run as a new round, which step 6's `profile.graderRounds` cap may forbid. End state: `grader-invalid` moves to branch 2. Its answer is the grader's turn: re-poked in the same round to rewrite its file in place (a rewrite after the dispatch closes the turn, judges.ts `checkJudgeReport`), or re-run as a new round only while `profile.graderRounds` leaves one (dispatch.md 'Round counting and escalation'); with no round left the task goes to the epic session, never to `gate run` and never to a builder. Branch 3 keeps `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `screenshots-missing` and `screenshots-stale`. Step 9 bounces a blocked outcome to the builder whose output its reason names: the tester for the two screenshots reasons; for `schema-invalid` and `artifacts-missing` the worker whose result the gate line's `--result` and `--agent` name; the coder for every other reason. A `grader-invalid` `gate-outcome` that reaches the log anyway is still a failed round the ladder counts as today; the grader's turn answers it, not a bounce, and it goes to the epic session. The mixed-case sentence in step 7 and in queue-and-gate.md names the three problems the code prints for a fresh grader file that is neither a list nor a grader document (the intake `judge-artifact`, then the stage problems `judges-outstanding` and `grader-invalid`, which test/cliResultsCheck.test.ts already pins), all branch 2. Task-7's criterion 5 kept step 9 unchanged; this task changes step 9's routing on purpose and leaves its env-failure bullet as it is. escalation.ts, gate.ts, judges.ts and paperwork.ts do not change. (b) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-fdeb317e, as revised by the pre-code review of the v6 draft (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9de7c928, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-c4cd9084, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-99d9be8b, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-817add66 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8afd5c81). The coder, tester and grader templates (the `handback-preflight` SHARED region) and wave.md step 8 (wave.md:462-468) say each worker's brief carries its filled `bs results check` line and the gate's check commands, but `composeBrief` (briefCompose.ts) writes neither and `lintDispatchPrompt` (dispatchLint.ts) checks for neither. End state, the reviewer's option (a): `bs brief compose` writes, for a coder, tester or grader brief, a `preflight` section holding the role's line with every value filled, and for a coder or tester a `gate_checks` section with the commands of the checks file the gate line takes, in the text form criterion 5 fixes; it refuses to compose such a brief without those values, and it runs the lint's own preflight check on the text it built and refuses one that fails it, so every brief it writes passes `bs dispatch lint`, as briefCompose.ts and the docs already promise. `bs dispatch lint` exits 1 on a coder, tester or grader brief, composed or hand-built, whose line is missing, ambiguous, for another task or role, or still holds a placeholder, and on a coder or tester brief that names no gate check. Compose already knows the task id, the role, the absolute worktree, the plan file it read, and the grader's declared artifact (`--artifact`, which is the grader file the line takes). It cannot know five values: the provider and the model tier the dispatch will use (the ladder may raise the tier), the coder's `--base`, the gate's checks file, and the work root `bs init` printed, which steps 5 and 7 write into every `--artifacts-dir`. Compose's own work root (paths.ts `WORK_ROOT`) follows its working directory and `BS_HOME`, so it is not used as a default. The five come from new flags, `--provider`, `--model-tier`, `--base`, `--checks` and `--work-root`, and wave.md step 8 passes `--work-root <work-root>`, the same value as steps 5 and 7. `--checks` is read with cli.ts `readChecksFile`, the gate's own intake; `--provider` and `--model-tier` are checked against taxonomy.yml's `provider` and `model_tier` (taxonomy.ts `loadTaxonomy`). Every value goes into the line through one shell-quoting function, so the shell reads each as one argument, and a value holding a newline or another control character is refused. The result file differs by role. No code computes a worker's result path today; the wave-runner names it, and state/results holds `<task>.json` for the coder beside `<task>.tester.json` for the tester, which run.md:437 reads as `state/results/<task-id>.tester*.json`. Yet bs-tester.md (bs-tester.md:144 and :200) and dispatch.md's return discipline (dispatch.md:141) tell the tester to write `state/results/<task-id>.json`, the coder's file. So the coder's result is `<work-root>/state/results/<task-id>.json` and the tester's is `<work-root>/state/results/<task-id>.tester.json`, in the composed line, in a `Result file:` line beside it, in bs-tester.md, in dispatch.md's return discipline and in wave.md step 5's record line, which is how the gate reads the tester's result. uiux is a builder with no `results check` mode, so its brief carries no line and the lint reports it not-applicable. To name the plan file it read, compose uses plan.ts `planFilePath`, which plan.ts now exports and otherwise leaves alone. The `handback-preflight` fragment and the coder and grader templates do not change: what they say becomes true. (c) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2afed53d. wave.md step 7 branch 4 bounds a return 'at most once per task' (wave.md:324) and then counts 'the returns per task and role' (wave.md:327-328), while queue-and-gate.md section 5 branch 4 (queue-and-gate.md:548-555) counts per task. End state: one counting rule, at most one branch-4 return per task whatever the worker's role, in one sentence both files carry word for word. (d) CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased` gains an entry for `task-8-close-review-r2-fixes`. The gate checks section marks each check the gate treats as heavy (testgate.ts `isHeavyCheck`) and its heading defers to the template's heavy-run section, so a full suite or e2e run never goes bare (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-65a64a1a); a check's command is listed verbatim, whatever it holds (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-32682fce). The wave-runner template, the agent-constraints standard and the uiux template say the tester's result file is its own (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9c6ba61f). (e) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7ec14864: the diff cap is sized from the claims, and an overrun is recorded, not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b, the routing in wave.md: step 7 branch 2 lists `grader-invalid` beside `judges-outstanding`, `uiux-spec-missing` and `uiux-visual-missing`, and says its answer is the grader's turn: re-poked in the same round to rewrite its file in place, or re-run as a new round only while step 6's `profile.graderRounds` leaves one, and with none left the epic session; never `gate run` and never a builder. Branch 3 lists exactly `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `screenshots-missing` and `screenshots-stale`. The mixed-case sentence says that a fresh grader file that is neither a list nor a grader document shows three problems, the intake `judge-artifact` and then the stage problems `judges-outstanding` and `grader-invalid`, all branch 2, and is never sent to `gate run`. Step 9 bounces a blocked outcome, on the same branch, to the builder whose output its reason names: the tester for `screenshots-missing` and `screenshots-stale` (it re-shoots at the gate's HEAD, step 5 records the new set, and step 5's uiux visual pass reviews it); for `schema-invalid` and `artifacts-missing` the worker whose result the gate line's `--result` and `--agent` name; the coder for every other reason. Step 9 also says that a `grader-invalid` `gate-outcome` in the log is still a failed round the ladder counts unchanged, is answered by the grader's turn and not by a bounce, and goes to the epic session; and that the ladder counts every blocked round whichever builder it bounces to, so from the second failed round the bounced builder, a tester included, runs on a strictly higher model tier (`checkModelTierRung`). Step 9's env-failure bullet is unchanged. The wave rule 'A blocked task blocks itself' names the task's builder, not its coder. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins each point: `grader-invalid` maps to branch 2 in the compiler-tied `REASON_BRANCH` map; every reason that map puts in branch 3 has its builder named in step 9, from a map whose keys are checked against the map's branch-3 reasons, so a reason moved into branch 3 without a builder fails; the three-problem mixed-case sentence; the grader-invalid-in-the-log sentence; the ladder sentence; the 'A blocked task blocks itself' wording. The existing env-failure assertions hold, and the word 'bounce' still appears in step 7 only inside branch 3.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b, the same routing in queue-and-gate.md: the outcome table's `grader-invalid` row says the grader's turn answers it (re-poked in the same round, or re-run within its round cap), never a builder, and that wave.md step 7 sends it to the grader before `gate run`; the table gains a `screenshots-missing` row and a `screenshots-stale` row, each a bounce to the tester; the `schema-invalid` row bounces to the worker whose result it is. Section 5's branch 2 and branch 3 lists and its mixed-case sentence match wave.md's (the same reasons in each branch, the same three problems), and its ladder paragraph says the ladder counts a tester bounce like a coder bounce. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins the three rows, and checks from the same `REASON_BRANCH` map that section 5 puts every `PaperworkReason` in the same branch as wave.md.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b, the ladder premise in code: test/handbackPreflight.test.ts runs the built `bs escalation check <session-id> --task <task-id>` over a session log in a `mkdtemp` state directory holding, in order, a coder `dispatch_decision` on `mid`, a tester `dispatch_decision` on `mid`, a blocked `gate-outcome` with reason `screenshots-missing`, a tester `dispatch_decision` on `mid`, a second blocked `gate-outcome` with reason `screenshots-missing`, and a tester `dispatch_decision` on `frontier`: it exits 0 and its tier-rung check is `ok`. The same log with that last tester dispatch on `mid` exits 1 and its tier-rung check is `violation`. This shows, with escalation.ts unchanged, that a screenshots block bounced to the tester is a counted round and that a tester dispatch answers the tier rung.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-1e8e9e9b, the grader premise in code: test/cliResultsCheck.test.ts, through the built CLI, with a recorded round-1 grader dispatch and a fresh grader file whose shape the gate blocks as `grader-invalid` but whose `structured_output.criteria` is an array (the 'grader criteria missing fields' or 'grader round 3' fixture of test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts, or one built the same way): the `--as gate` preflight shows the stage problem `grader-invalid` and no `intake` problem. After that same file is rewritten in place as a valid grader document with a later mtime, and no new judge dispatch is recorded, the `--as gate` preflight shows no `grader` and no `judges` problem, and the log holds one grader dispatch for the task and no `gate-outcome`: branch 2's same-round re-poke needs no new round. On a separate scratch session with the same `grader-invalid` file, `gate run` on the same line blocks with reason `grader-invalid`, writes a blocked `gate-outcome` that `readFailedRounds` counts, and leaves no grader turn outstanding (`bs judge outstanding --task <task-id>` exits 0); that is why branch 2 settles `grader-invalid` before `gate run`.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-fdeb317e, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9de7c928, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-c4cd9084, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-99d9be8b f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8afd5c81, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-65a64a1a, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-32682fce and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-13606fd6, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b954029f and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7a110665, the composer: `composeBrief` writes, for a coder, tester or grader brief, a `preflight` section after `envelope`, in this text form: for a coder or tester, first the line `Result file: <absolute path>`; then the line `Hand-back preflight line (run it as your last step, exactly as written):`; then the role's `bs results check <task-id> --as <role>` line on its own line, with the flags, in order, of that role's line in wave.md step 8: coder `--result --agent coder --provider --model-tier --worktree --base --artifacts-dir`; tester `--result --agent tester --provider --model-tier --plan --artifacts-dir`; grader `--grader --artifacts-dir`. The coder's `--result` and `Result file:` are `<work-root>/state/results/<task-id>.json`; the tester's are `<work-root>/state/results/<task-id>.tester.json`, never the coder's file. `--artifacts-dir` is `<work-root>/state/artifacts`, `--worktree` the brief's worktree, `--plan` the plan file compose read, `--grader` the declared artifact, and `--provider`, `--model-tier`, `--base` and `--work-root` the new options; `<work-root>` is the `--work-root` value, never compose's own work root; every path is absolute and `<task-id>` is the plan's qualified id: `--worktree` and `--artifact` keep their existing refusals of a relative path (`brief.worktree-required`, `brief.artifact-required`), a relative `--work-root` is refused as `brief.invalid-value` naming `--work-root`, because compose reads nothing there to resolve it against, and the plan path is the absolute path of the plan file compose read, so a relative `--plan` or `--specs-dir` still composes an absolute `--plan`. A coder or tester brief also gets a `gate_checks` section after `preflight`: the line `Gate checks (run each over the whole project before you hand back; run a check marked heavy as your template's heavy-run section says, never bare):`; then, for each check of the checks file in file order, the line `- <name>:`, or `- <name> (heavy):` when testgate.ts `isHeavyCheck` says the gate treats it as heavy, followed by every line of its command, verbatim, each prefixed by exactly four spaces (a blank command line is written as the four spaces alone). The heading and the marker name no tool, package manager or test runner. Every value in the preflight line, the task id included, goes through one shell-quoting function: a value made only of `A-Za-z0-9_./:@%+=,-` is written bare, any other is wrapped in single quotes with each `'` inside it written `'\''`. Compose refuses, after every existing refusal so each existing refusal keeps its code: a coder brief without `--provider`, `--model-tier`, `--base`, `--work-root` or a checks file holding at least one check, a tester brief without `--provider`, `--model-tier`, `--work-root` or such a checks file, and a grader brief without `--work-root`, as `brief.preflight-values-required` naming each missing flag; a `--provider` outside taxonomy.yml's `provider` or a `--model-tier` outside its `model_tier` (read with taxonomy.ts `loadTaxonomy`), any value it writes into the preflight line (the task id, a flag value or a path) that is blank, holds a newline or another control character, or holds a `<...>` token, and a check name that is blank or holds a newline or another control character, as `brief.invalid-value` naming the flag or the check and, for the two vocabularies, the allowed values. A check's command is never refused for what it holds: a `<...>` token or a line break in it is written verbatim, as `gate run` runs it. A check whose `cmd` is missing, not a string, empty or only whitespace is refused as `brief.invalid-value` naming the check and its `cmd` field: cli.ts `readChecksFile` accepts such a check, but `gate run` cannot run the first three (node's `spawn` throws on a missing, non-string or empty command, so the gate ends in an error, not an outcome) and runs the last as a no-op that checks nothing, so no brief lists one. Last, it runs the lint's own preflight check on the text it built and refuses with `brief.preflight-unlintable`, carrying the lint's status, unless that is `ok` or `not-applicable`, as it already refuses `brief.turn-budget-ambiguous`; so `bs brief compose` never exits 0 with a brief `bs dispatch lint` refuses. Every other role's brief is unchanged, section for section. `bs brief compose` takes `--provider <name> --model-tier <tier> --base <ref> --checks <file> --work-root <dir>`, reads `--checks` with cli.ts `readChecksFile` so a bad file fails as it does for `gate run`, and usage.ts lists the flags. test/briefCompose.test.ts pins each value, the coder's and the tester's result files (different, each equal to its line's `--result`), each refusal with its code and the flags it names, the `gate_checks` form with a heavy and a light check (`unit` and `lint` unmarked, a `lint` check with `"heavy": true` and a `test` check with `"heavy": false`, each marked as `isHeavyCheck` says), a check command holding `<...>` and a line break that composes and is listed verbatim, each refused check shape (`cmd` missing, `7`, empty, whitespace only) with the check's name in the error, a relative `--work-root` refused by name, a relative `--plan` composing an absolute `--plan`, the absolute paths, unchanged reviewer and uiux briefs, and a work root holding a space and a single quote, which appears in the line as one single-quoted word; it reads the role's line from wave.md step 8 and from the role's template and requires the same flag names in the same order as the composed line, so the three copies cannot drift. test/cliOptimize.test.ts, through the built CLI with `BS_HOME` in a `mkdtemp` directory: composes a coder, a tester and a grader brief with every value given, under a `--work-root` whose path holds a space, requires that each composed `--artifacts-dir` equal the `--artifacts-dir` of wave.md step 7's `gate run` line read from the file with its `<work-root>` filled by the same value, and runs each composed line through `/bin/sh -c` with `bs` resolved to the built CLI, requiring a paperwork document whose `as` is the role and whose `artifact_home` sits under that spaced work root, never an `error` document; and shows that compose without `--provider` exits 1 with `brief.preflight-values-required` naming `--provider` and writes no `--out` file.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-fdeb317e, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-817add66, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8afd5c81, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-65a64a1a and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7a110665, the lint: dispatchLint.ts exports one preflight check, which `lintDispatchPrompt` and `composeBrief` both call, and the lint report gains one key, `preflight`, holding `status`, the line it read and, for a coder or tester, the number of gate checks. For a coder, tester or grader prompt it reads the standalone lines (the whole line is the command, optionally in backticks) that start with `bs results check`, the way `parseStatedTurns` reads the turn budget, so a line quoted inside the spec JSON or a lesson does not count, and splits the line by the quoting rule of criterion 5: none is `missing`; more than one is `ambiguous`; a line whose task id does not match `--task` by taskId.ts `taskIdsMatch` (a bare and a qualified spelling of one id match) or whose `--as` is not `--role` is `mismatch`; a line holding any `<...>` token is `placeholder`; a coder or tester prompt without the heading line `Gate checks (run each over the whole project before you hand back; run a check marked heavy as your template's heavy-run section says, never bare):`, or with no counted check in the section under it (which runs while each line is a `- ` check line or starts with four spaces), is `no-checks`; a `- ` check line counts only when at least one of the four-space command lines under it holds a character other than a space, so a check with no command is never counted; otherwise `ok`. Every other role, uiux included, is `not-applicable`. Each of `missing`, `ambiguous`, `mismatch`, `placeholder` and `no-checks` makes `exitCode` 1; the turns and artifact checks and their statuses are unchanged. test/dispatchLint.test.ts pins every status and its exit code, `no-checks` for a hand-built brief whose only check line has no command or a blank one; the `not-applicable` roles; a brief composed and linted with the bare task id (`--epic` given) that lints `ok`; a line whose single-quoted path holds a space, read as one value; and a composed coder brief whose spec quotes a full `bs results check` line mid-text and still lints `ok`. It runs `bs dispatch lint` through the built CLI on a composed coder brief (exit 0) and on the same brief with its `--provider` value replaced by `<name>`, as a hand-built brief would carry it (exit 1, `placeholder`).

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-fdeb317e, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9de7c928, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-c4cd9084 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8afd5c81, the docs: wave.md step 8 says that `bs brief compose` writes each coder's, tester's and grader's filled preflight line, and each coder's and tester's gate check commands, from the flags it names (`--provider`, `--model-tier`, `--base` for the coder, `--checks` with the file step 7's gate line takes, and `--work-root <work-root>`, the same value as steps 5 and 7), that it refuses to compose such a brief without them, and that `bs dispatch lint` exits 1 on a brief that lacks them; its three per-role lines stay as written, so task-7's test still runs exactly seven concrete lines. wave.md step 5 names the tester's result file `<work-root>/state/results/<task-id>.tester.json`. dispatch.md 'Carry into the prompt' lists the line and the check commands among what compose emits, shows the text form of the `preflight` and `gate_checks` sections from criterion 5 (the two heading lines, the `Result file:` line, the `- <name>:` and `- <name> (heavy):` lines and the four-space command lines) so a hand-built brief can satisfy the lint, and names the new compose refusals and lint failures beside the turn and artifact ones; dispatch.md's return discipline says the tester writes `state/results/<task-id>.tester.json`, never the coder's file. bs-tester.md, outside its SHARED regions, names `state/results/<task-id>.tester.json` where it says where to write the result and in its return line. The same correction reaches every sibling sentence (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9c6ba61f), each outside its file's SHARED regions and naming no tool: bs-wave-runner.md's return-discipline bullet and docs/standards/agent-constraints.md's return-discipline bullet say a tester writes `state/results/<task-id>.tester.json`, and bs-uiux.md no longer calls the bare `state/results/<task-id>.json` the tester's result path. docs/guide/operator-guide/worktrees-and-judges.md section 3d names the new flags, sections and refusals, and its `bs dispatch lint` output example carries the `preflight` key. queue-and-gate.md section 5 says the composer writes the line and the lint fails a brief without it. The `handback-preflight` fragment and the coder and grader templates do not change. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins each of these statements; checks that the tester's result path is the same in bs-tester.md, bs-wave-runner.md, bs-uiux.md, docs/standards/agent-constraints.md, wave.md step 5, dispatch.md and the line compose writes, that no file in .claude/agents, .claude/skills/bs or docs/standards still says every worker or the tester writes the bare `state/results/<task-id>.json`, that wave.md step 8's compose example carries `--work-root <work-root>`, and that run.md's `state/results/<task-id>.tester*.json` matches it; and checks that the keys of the worktrees-and-judges.md lint example are the keys of a real `lintDispatchPrompt` report.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2afed53d: wave.md step 7 branch 4 and queue-and-gate.md section 5 branch 4 carry one and the same counting sentence, word for word: at most one branch-4 return per task, whatever the worker's role, counted as the task's builder dispatches whose `causal_parent` is such an `error-logged` event, and a second `result` problem on the same task, from any worker, goes to the epic session, which returns it no more without the operator's answer. Neither file says 'per task and role' or counts branch-4 returns per role anywhere, and queue-and-gate.md's later sentence on branch 4's bound (a playbook rule the log evidences by structure and no verb enforces) says per task. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts finds the sentence in both files after collapsing whitespace and requires the two equal, checks that neither file contains 'task and role', and keeps every existing branch-4 assertion (`at most once per task`, the fields, the `causal_parent` link, `continuation_of`, the epic-session sentence).
